content:
As WhatsApp prepares to officially roll out its username feature, the messaging app now allows users to save a contact's username alongside their name and phone number. Here's what you need to know.

A username field for new contacts has started rolling out to some WhatsApp users

While usernames are a common feature on most messaging platforms, WhatsApp has only recently begun moving away from its long-standing practice of identifying users solely by phone number.

WhatsApp previously started rolling out a username reservation system, giving users a chance to secure their preferred handle before the feature officially launches, to prevent others from impersonating them.

A few weeks ago, WhatsApp began enabling the username feature for some iPhone users.

Now, according to WABetaInfo, WhatsApp has started adding a username field when users add new contacts. The field appears between the name field and the phone number field.

Here's the report from WABetaInfo:

WABetaInfo noted that the username field appears to be rolling out to some users on both the WhatsApp beta and stable versions.

When testing on the latest stable version, the field was visible, but even when entering an actual existing username, the system still displayed a message saying "this username is not on WhatsApp".

That said, this is another step forward for WhatsApp as it catches up with its competitors and adds what many consider a long-overdue basic feature.
